key_insight: VideoWorld 2 shows that decoupling action dynamics from visual appearance—via a dynamic-enhanced Latent Dynamics Model (dLDM) combined with a pretrained video diffusion model—lets agents learn transferable knowledge directly from raw real-world videos.
problem_solved: How to learn transferable, actionable knowledge from unlabeled, visually diverse real-world videos so that policies or dynamics models generalize to new environments without costly labels or simulators.
method: Introduce dLDM that models action dynamics in a latent space separately from visual appearance.
Leverage a pretrained video diffusion model to handle realistic visual generation/appearance, while dLDM focuses on dynamics.
Train on large-scale unlabeled real-world videos to produce dynamics representations that transfer to downstream control or decision tasks.
impact: Enables practitioners to use abundant unlabeled video data to pretrain transferable dynamics models, improving sample efficiency and cross-domain generalization for embodied agents and downstream RL/vision tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram illustrating: raw video -> pretrained video diffusion (appearance) + dLDM (dynamics) -> transferable latent representation -> downstream task/policy
Side-by-side examples showing the same dynamics rendered with different visual appearances to illustrate decoupling
Bar chart or table comparing transfer performance (e.g., sample efficiency or success rate) of models pre-trained on real videos vs. baselines
Latent-space visualization (e.g., t-SNE/UMAP) showing dynamics clusters that are invariant to visual domain
paper_title: VideoWorld 2: Learning Transferable Knowledge from Real-world Videos
paper_authors: Zhongwei Ren, Yunchao Wei, Xiao Yu, Guixun Luo, Yao Zhao
